desk.headline: Revenue up 28% to $6.3bn and adjusted EBITDA up 50% to $2.4bn; 2026 range narrowed with higher midpoint, 2027 outlook initiated
results: Operating revenue rose 28% to $6.3bn; Ongoing Operations adjusted EBITDA jumped 50% to $2.4bn on higher realised power and capacity prices, the Lotus plants and Martin Lake Unit 1 returning.
Net income was $1.14bn, including a $559m unrealised hedge gain, partly offset by a $269m impairment at Moss Landing 350.
Texas and East segments drove the gain; fleet commercial availability was nearly 95% through record summer heat.
Closed the ~5,500 MW Cogentrix gas fleet deal in October and redeemed all $1bn of Series A preferred stock.
Board added $1.5bn to buybacks, leaving ~$2.5bn to use by end-2028; ~$6.7bn bought back since Nov 2021.

guidance.summary: Vistra narrowed its 2026 ranges and raised the midpoints, and gave its first 2027 ranges, which include Cogentrix. The company does not guide on EPS.

items.metric: Ongoing Ops adjusted FCF before growth
Ongoing Ops adjusted FCF before growth

points: Management kept its view of strong load growth through 2030 (4–6% a year in ERCOT, 2–3% in PJM), while flagging softer near-term Texas power forwards.
Data-centre talks are active at existing nuclear and gas plants and new builds; customers are more open to bridge options such as behind-the-meter supply.
Cogentrix cost about $4bn net (~$729/kW) and is expected to add to free cash flow per share right away.
Plans assume roughly $3bn a year of buybacks over 2027–2030 and at least $1bn a year through 2028; pro forma leverage is about 2.8x.
Risks named: a possible Texas data-centre moratorium, permit holds in ERCOT and slow PJM contracting; 2028 is ~78% hedged but less so in ERCOT.
